## Overview

Put the GDN metadata of batches with prefills (mixed steps) into persistent, padded buffers, and give the GDN prefill kernels a static-grid mode (FLA `use_graph`, `causal_conv1d_fn(num_programs=...)`). The eager forward does not change. This is the first of two PRs to run the GDN core inside a CUDA graph in mixed steps; the second is #61952. Kernel form ported from FLA [#1212](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/pull/1212) (merged, KDA) and [#1230](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/pull/1230) (GDN, open). Related: SGLang issue [#35851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35851) (same per-layer break cost). Nearby open PRs that touch the same files but do something else: #60659 (FLA prefill checkpoints), #61434 (deferred spec-decode state stores), #38315 (fused kkt + solve_tril).

## Claims

- `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` puts every mixed-batch field at a fixed address: state indices, cu_seqlens (spec / non-spec / prefill), `num_accepted_tokens`, `has_initial_state` (all / prefill), token indices, FLA `chunk_indices` / `chunk_offsets`, causal_conv1d `batch_ptr` / `token_chunk_offset_ptr`. The rows after the real rows hold documented pads (`MIXED_BATCH_PAD_VALUES`), so a padded view of any length is valid for a static grid.
- The FLA GDN chunk kernels (cumsum, kkt, solve_tril, wy_fast, chunk_o) skip `[-1, 0]` sentinel chunks when `use_graph=True`. `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` needs no change: a zero-length padded sequence writes its initial state as its final state.
- `causal_conv1d_fn` can launch a static program count; the existing `PAD_SLOT_ID` exit handles the extra programs.
- No behaviour change: the staged fields keep their length, values and dtype. The causal_conv1d program buffers (`batch_ptr`, `token_chunk_offset_ptr`) now have the capacity length instead of a new `max(1024, n) * 2` allocation; the kernel reads only the first `nums_dict[8]["tot"]` entries and the rest are `PAD_SLOT_ID`, as before. The NVIDIA Kimi-K3 KDA builder, which computes its own conv metadata, uses the same buffers. All new arguments default to the old path. No new host sync, no new H2D copy, fewer per-step device allocations.

## Validation

- CPU (macOS, Python 3.13, torch 2.10, CPU platform), one run of `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`, `test_gdn_zero_draft_spec_rows.py`, `test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py`, `test_mamba_metadata_builder.py`, `test_mamba2_prefill_checkpoints.py`, `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py`, `test_gdn_static_grid.py`: **80 passed**, 18 skipped (GPU-only), 11 failed. The 11 failures are all in `test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py` and fail the same way on `origin/main` in this environment ("Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled"). The GDN builder files alone: 66 passed on `origin/main`, 66 + 6 new passed with this PR. A mutation check (pad fill removed, or chunk pad set to 0) makes all 6 new tests fail. Note: the local run uses import stubs for `compressed_tensors` / `torchvision` and `--noconftest`; CI does not need them.
- Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. `mypy` on the three changed backend/op files: no new errors (31 on main, 25 after).
- GPU (1 × A100-SXM4-40GB): this branch backported onto an older main (5555a2d8f, only docstring and import conflicts) to match the available image, so every changed file is checked against the image copy before the PR files are laid over. `tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py`, `test_gdn_prefill_flashinfer.py`, `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py`, `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`: **265 passed** without this PR; the same files plus the new `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_static_grid.py`: **286 passed** with it. The static-grid test checks the static FLA forward and the static `causal_conv1d_fn` against the batch-sized ones, bitwise on real rows (1 / 7 / 64 sequences, 1-2048 tokens, bf16 / fp32 state, with / without initial state). A first GPU run found that the NVIDIA KDA builder did not use the new conv buffers (2 KDA test failures); fixed in the last commit.
- Performance: this PR alone changes no forward path, so it gives no speed-up by itself. Expected eager cost: one copy plus one pad fill per staged field, about 10 small launches per non-spec mixed step and about 22 with spec decodes, estimated below 0.1 ms of host time per step (**estimate**).
- Serving, together with #61952 (this PR + #61952, backported onto 5555a2d8f). Setup: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (36 GDN + 12 sparse-attention layers, MTP 3), TP8 + EP, DCP 4, 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, prefix caching (Mamba `align`), MLPerf agentic multi-turn workload, 32 concurrent sessions, 1 × 60 min per arm, two pairs on two nodes (the second pair in reversed arm order). TTFT/TPOT from a full replay of every request with the Endpoints client's own TPOT code:

  | Pair | Arm | TTFT P50 / P95 / P99 | TPOT P50 / P95 / P99 | Requests/s |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | without | 978 / 1,816 / 2,730 ms | 17.6 / 26.4 / 31.9 ms | 2.86 |
  | 1 | with both PRs | 926 / 2,335 / 7,811 ms* | 16.0 / 26.1 / 38.8 ms | 2.98 |
  | 2 | with both PRs | 943 / 1,972 / 3,659 ms | 15.7 / 24.5 / 32.7 ms | 3.09 |
  | 2 | without | 954 / 1,743 / 2,571 ms | 17.6 / 26.3 / 31.0 ms | 2.89 |

  \* includes a 160 s window in which requests did not reach the engine (the engine was idle; cause not found).

  Both pairs: TPOT P50 −9 to −10 %, requests/s +4 to +7 %. The TTFT tail is worse in both pairs (P95 +13 % in pair 2). A third run of the "with" arm on another day gave TTFT P95 1,829 ms, so the tail moves by about as much between runs as between arms; no TTFT change is claimed.

## Details

**Motivation (measured from nsys traces, our deployment, C32, DCP 4, 8x A100).** A mixed step is host-bound: 99.6 ms of host time (p50, NVTX range) against a GPU compute bound of about 65-70 ms. The GDN eager breaks take 55.2 ms of that host time and 720 of 1,348 launches (20 launches per layer, 36 layers). nsys adds a fixed cost per API call, so 55.2 ms is an upper bound for an unprofiled run. In FULL decode steps the GDN core is already captured; in mixed steps `eager_break_during_capture` runs it eagerly because its metadata is new in every step and its grids depend on the batch.

**What this PR does not do.** The forward stays eager and `_cudagraph_support` stays `UNIFORM_BATCH`. #61952 adds a branch-free mixed forward on the padded views and removes the eager break when the static form applies. `build_for_cudagraph_capture` keeps its decode-only check: with `UNIFORM_BATCH` no caller can reach a mixed capture yet, so a worst-case mixed form would be dead code in this PR.

**Design.**
- One buffer per field, sized by `max_num_seqs` and `max_num_batched_tokens`; chunk capacity `cdiv(T, 64) + S - 1`, conv program capacity `cdiv(T, 8) + S - 1` (each sequence adds at most one partial chunk or program). The `_stage()` helper (copy to the front, fill pads, return the view) also replaces the existing FULL-decode staging code. The decode buffers do not change, so subclasses that size their staging by them (Kimi-K3 KDA) do not change.
- FLA chunk metadata is padded on the CPU and goes to its buffer with one H2D copy per tensor, as before, but into a persistent buffer instead of a new device tensor.
- Pads: `NULL_BLOCK_ID` state indices (pad rows touch only the null block), repeated last cu_seqlens value (zero-length sequences), `has_initial_state=False`, `num_accepted_tokens=1`, token index 0, chunk `[-1, 0]`, conv `PAD_SLOT_ID`.
- Kernel form follows FLA: a `USE_GRAPH` constexpr and `if USE_GRAPH and i_n < 0: return`. `USE_GRAPH` is not an autotune key, so graph mode reuses tuned configs (it compiles one more variant; warm it up before capture). Unlike FLA, uncovered output rows stay `torch.empty`: inference reads only real rows.

**Limitations.**
- Static chunk metadata covers the default Triton/FLA prefill path. FlashInfer (no FLA chunk metadata), CuteDSL and AITER FlyDSL keep their own metadata, and subclasses that override `_build_chunk_metadata` (KDA) keep new tensors.
- Mamba prefix-caching checkpoint metadata (`align` mode) and the FlashInfer checkpoint plan are not staged.
- `spec_sequence_masks` in mixed batches is not staged (the forward uses it only as a flag).

@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Static (CUDA graph) grids of the GDN prefill kernels.
+
+A static grid covers the largest batch: padded tokens, zero-length padded
+sequences and ``[-1, 0]`` padded chunks for FLA, ``PAD_SLOT_ID`` programs for
+causal_conv1d. On the real rows it must give the same bits as the batch-sized
+grid.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.causal_conv1d import causal_conv1d_fn
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops import chunk_gated_delta_rule
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.index import (
+    prepare_chunk_indices,
+    prepare_chunk_offsets,
+)
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import CAUSAL_CONV1D_BLOCK_M
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import compute_causal_conv1d_metadata
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda_alike(), reason="GDN Triton kernels need a GPU"
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+CHUNK_SIZE = 64
+# Static capacity beyond the real batch.
+NUM_PAD_SEQS = 5
+NUM_PAD_TOKENS = 100
+
+
+def _seq_lens(num_seqs: int, generator: torch.Generator) -> list[int]:
+    # Chunk-boundary lengths first, then random lengths in [1, 2048].
+    edges = [1, 2048, 63, 64, 65, 129]
+    random = torch.randint(1, 2049, (num_seqs,), generator=generator).tolist()
+    return (edges + random)[:num_seqs]
+
+
+def _cu_seqlens(seq_lens: list[int], num_padded_seqs: int = 0) -> torch.Tensor:
+    lens = torch.tensor(seq_lens + [0] * num_padded_seqs, dtype=torch.int32)
+    return F.pad(lens.cumsum(0, dtype=torch.int32), (1, 0)).to(DEVICE)
+
+
+def _pad_chunk_indices(chunk_indices: torch.Tensor, num_rows: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    pad = chunk_indices.new_tensor((-1, 0)).expand(num_rows - len(chunk_indices), 2)
+    return torch.cat([chunk_indices, pad])
+
+
+def _conv_metadata(nums_dict, batch_ptr, token_chunk_offset_ptr) -> SimpleNamespace:
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        nums_dict=nums_dict,
+        batch_ptr=batch_ptr,
+        token_chunk_offset_ptr=token_chunk_offset_ptr,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_initial_state", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("state_dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_seqs", [1, 7, 64])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_chunk_gated_delta_rule_static_grid_is_bitwise_equal(
+    num_seqs: int, state_dtype: torch.dtype, with_initial_state: bool
+):
+    rng_cpu = torch.Generator().manual_seed(num_seqs)
+    rng = torch.Generator(DEVICE).manual_seed(num_seqs)
+    seq_lens = _seq_lens(num_seqs, rng_cpu)
+    num_tokens = sum(seq_lens)
+    num_padded_tokens = num_tokens + NUM_PAD_TOKENS
+    max_num_seqs = num_seqs + NUM_PAD_SEQS
+    num_k_heads, num_v_heads, head_dim = 2, 4, 128
+
+    def randn(*shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+        return torch.randn(*shape, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype, generator=rng)
+
+    q = F.normalize(randn(1, num_padded_tokens, num_k_heads, head_dim), dim=-1)
+    k = F.normalize(randn(1, num_padded_tokens, num_k_heads, head_dim), dim=-1)
+    v = randn(1, num_padded_tokens, num_v_heads, head_dim)
+    g = F.logsigmoid(randn(1, num_padded_tokens, num_v_heads, dtype=torch.float32))
+    beta = randn(1, num_padded_tokens, num_v_heads, dtype=torch.float32).sigmoid()
+    h0 = randn(max_num_seqs, num_v_heads, head_dim, head_dim, dtype=state_dtype)
+
+    cu_seqlens = _cu_seqlens(seq_lens)
+    o, final_state = chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+        q=q[:, :num_tokens],
+        k=k[:, :num_tokens],
+        v=v[:, :num_tokens],
+        g=g[:, :num_tokens],
+        beta=beta[:, :num_tokens],
+        initial_state=h0[:num_seqs] if with_initial_state else None,
+        output_final_state=True,
+        cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+        chunk_indices=prepare_chunk_indices(cu_seqlens, CHUNK_SIZE),
+        chunk_offsets=prepare_chunk_offsets(cu_seqlens, CHUNK_SIZE),
+    )
+
+    static_cu_seqlens = _cu_seqlens(seq_lens, NUM_PAD_SEQS)
+    max_num_chunks = cdiv(num_padded_tokens, CHUNK_SIZE) + max_num_seqs - 1
+    static_o, static_final_state = chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+        q=q,
+        k=k,
+        v=v,
+        g=g,
+        beta=beta,
+        initial_state=h0 if with_initial_state else None,
+        output_final_state=True,
+        cu_seqlens=static_cu_seqlens,
+        chunk_indices=_pad_chunk_indices(
+            prepare_chunk_indices(cu_seqlens, CHUNK_SIZE), max_num_chunks
+        ),
+        chunk_offsets=prepare_chunk_offsets(static_cu_seqlens, CHUNK_SIZE),
+        use_graph=True,
+    )
+
+    assert torch.equal(static_o[:, :num_tokens], o)
+    assert torch.equal(static_final_state[:num_seqs], final_state)
+    # A zero-length sequence returns its initial state.
+    expected_pad_state = (
+        h0[num_seqs:].float()
+        if with_initial_state
+        else torch.zeros_like(static_final_state[num_seqs:])
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(static_final_state[num_seqs:], expected_pad_state)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_seqs", [1, 7, 64])
